target_customer: Individual Mac users with overloaded inboxes
problem: Inboxes fill with cold outreach and newsletters that bury important mail. Alrighty filters unwanted mail and lets users connect their own AI tools to what matters.
business_model: consumer email app, free plan with no time limit; paid tiers not described

founders.name: Emmett Miller
founders.background_notes: Bio on YC page: wants to make the world better with innovative tools.

founders.background_notes: Listed only as co-founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Leo Schottenstein
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as a founder but also shows a team size of 2 and what looks like mixed content from another company, so the founder list is uncertain.

competitors.name: Superhuman
competitors.funding_then: $33M Series B in 2019 at a reported $260M valuation

technical_complexity.rationale: A native mail client on top of Gmail, iCloud and Outlook protocols is moderate engineering; the AI features use existing models.

defensibility.rationale: Many well-funded email clients exist and the filtering features are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows what incumbents did to Alrighty; the product appears to have been rebuilt around AI agents by 2026.

market_need_then: Email overload and cold outreach were widely discussed, and a market of paid clients existed in 2021, but no source on Alrighty's own demand was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: short, direct and confident; plain-language headings such as Email, fixed

branding.brand_signature: the mail app that pushes back

brand_strength.rationale: A casual, friendly name but no press or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Very little is public about Alrighty. It is listed as active with a team of two, backed by Y Combinator, and its current site markets a Mac and Linux mail app with an optional AI agent. No funding, traction or outcome was found, so the trajectory cannot be judged and the 2021 batch product may differ from the current one.
